focus: A5 agents: can one .skilled/agents/*.md frontmatter block serve OpenCode v1 1.19.3 and v2 2.0.32 with identical intent

graphEvents.label: Can one agent frontmatter serve v1 and v2?
v1 and v2 agent field namespaces differ; v2 translates from v1 one-way
chrome_devtools deny is inert on v2; add browser deny
Frontmatter must be authored in v1 shape

label: v1 and v2 use disjoint agent field namespaces and v2 translates v1 frontmatter one-way: v1 resolves {name,mode,permission,options,native,prompt,description,temperature,tools} (observed via `opencode debug agent markdown`), v2's Config.AgentEncoded is only {model,request,system,description,mode,hidden,color,steps,disabled,permissions}. v2 does not parse our files as v2 keys, it translates them (write/edit/patch collapse to edit, bash to shell, task to subagent) and appends its own defaults. Therefore a single frontmatter block is viable only in the v1 shape with v2-only fields as tolerated extras; a v2 `permissions:` list is not a safe common denominator.

`temperature` survives into v2 only as request.body.temperature, which v2 does not send yet: the v2 record for agent `code` is {"request":{"body":{"temperature":0.1}}} while built-in `build` has an empty body. Ten of the twelve repo agents declare temperature 0.1 and depend on deterministic sampling, so per-agent sampling is a v1-only guarantee and no frontmatter change can restore it on v2.

`chrome_devtools: deny` protects nothing on v2 and `browser: deny` must be added beside it: v2's action vocabulary (read off its built-in agents) is *, read, question, edit, shell, webfetch, doom_loop, external_directory, browser, subagent, so chrome_devtools, grep, glob, list survive as inert rules (ai-council's v2 record still carries {"action":"chrome_devtools","effect":"deny"}). The fix is safe on both hosts because v1 has no fixed permission-key enum — it emitted rules literally named chrome_devtools, list and patch from our frontmatter — so `browser: deny` is a real denial on v2 and a harmless inert rule on v1.

v1 auto-derives a `tools` enable map from the permission map and v2 has no `tools` key at all: no repo agent declares `tools:` yet v1 resolves one with task:false, webfetch:false, todowrite:true, skill:true, etc. A tool switched off on v1 without a permission rule is impossible to express on v2, where only permission rules exist. The current twelve agents are unaffected because their behaviour is already permission-encoded.

Agent bodies name the v1 Task tool as a proper noun and v2 ships the body verbatim as `system`: `Task` appears 30x in orchestrate, 12x in ai-council, 7x in debug, 4x in markdown and deep-review, and 3x or fewer elsewhere. `.skilled/agents/code.md:54` tells the reader that `permission.task: deny` blocks the Task tool, which is only true under v1 naming on v2 (the mapping to the `subagent` action is proven by v2's record). `.skilled/agents/orchestrate.md:35` already carries a per-runtime delegation-tool table but lists four runtimes and gets OpenCode wrong for v2, so the fix is to generalize the noun and add the v1/v2 split rather than fork the body.

v2-only agent fields cannot be used as a common denominator until v1 tolerance is probed, and `steps` has no dual-version story at all: hidden, color, steps and disabled exist on v2 and appear nowhere in v1's resolved key set, so a per-agent step cap can be expressed on v2 only. markdown.md already uses `mode: all`, which v1 accepts verbatim; v2's built-ins only show primary and subagent, so v2's handling of `all` is unverified.

The v1-tolerance question was not settled this iteration because the probe project it needs is outside the research packet's write authority: whether v1 strips, ignores or misreads a v2 `permissions:` list and the keys steps/hidden/color/disabled, and whether v1 forwards unknown frontmatter keys into provider `options`, all remain UNVERIFIED. The refused probe was recorded as a scope violation with its exact command rather than executed.
v1.19.3 `opencode debug agent markdown` resolves an agent to {name,mode,permission,options,native,prompt,description,temperature,tools} with permission as a resolved rule array and options {}
v2.0.32 `/api/agent` returns Agent.Info records for the repo agents with permissions translated from the v1 permission map and temperature moved into request.body
committed v2 OpenAPI dump declares Config.AgentEncoded with exactly model,request,system,description,mode,hidden,color,steps,disabled,permissions
`.opencode/agents` is a symlink to ../.skilled/agents and both hosts read the same 12 agent files plus README.txt
Agent frontmatter must be authored in the v1 shape, because only v1-to-v2 translation is demonstrated; v2-only fields may be added only alongside their v1 equivalents.

Every constraint expressed with an action name that exists on only one host must be paired with that host's name for the same capability (chrome_devtools/browser, task/subagent, bash/shell, patch/edit), since neither host errors on an unknown permission name and so a missing pair fails silently.

direction: Author agent frontmatter in the v2 shape with a `permissions:` rule list as the shared form for both hosts
reason: v2 is demonstrated to translate v1-shaped frontmatter into v2 permissions, but nothing shows v1 reading a v2 `permissions:` list, and v1's own resolved shape has no such key. Choosing the v2 shape would rest on an unverified assumption for v1 while discarding a proven translation for v2.
